knowledge:
- key_parameters: data=The associated dataset in long format ;; geom=The ggplot2 geom function to use for plotting (e.g., geom_star, geom_tile, geom_col) ;; mapping=Aesthetic mappings, where y must map to the tip labels ;; position=Position adjustment (e.g., "identity" to place points directly on tip nodes) ;; offset=The distance between external layers (default is 0.03 times x range of tree) ;; pwidth=Width of the external layer (default is 0.2 times x range of tree) ;; axis.params=List of parameters to add and customize the axis of an external layer ;; grid.params=List of parameters to add background grid lines to an external layer
- alternatives: geom_facet in ggtree (only works with rectangular, roundrect, ellipse, and slanted layouts; use ggtreeExtra for circular, fan, and radial layouts)
- when_to_use: When visualizing multiple associated datasets (such as heatmaps, bar charts, or star plots) on the outer rings of a phylogenetic tree, particularly in circular, fan, or radial layouts.
- pitfalls: Input datasets must be in long format (use melt or pivot_longer if in short format) ;; If not using the %<+% operator to merge data, you must specify the tip label column in the y aesthetic of geom_fruit (e.g., y=ID) ;; When mapping multiple variables to the same aesthetic (like fill) across different layers, you must use new_scale_fill() from ggnewscale to reset the scale ;; In geom_fruit_list, the first element must be a geom_fruit layer.

workflows.name: sequential_external_layers
workflows.intent: Align multiple sequential data layers (such as tip points, heatmaps, and bar charts) to the outer rings of a phylogenetic tree.
input: tree_tippoint_bar.csv (CSV containing tip annotations like Location, Length, Group, Abundance)
workflows.stages: 1. Read the phylogenetic tree using read.tree ;; 2. Read the associated datasets using read.csv ;; 3. Initialize the tree plot using ggtree with a circular/fan layout ;; 4. Add the first layer (star points) using geom_fruit with position="identity" ;; 5. Reset the fill scale using new_scale_fill() ;; 6. Add the second layer (discrete heatmap) using geom_fruit with geom=geom_tile ;; 7. Reset the fill scale using new_scale_fill() ;; 8. Add the third layer (continuous heatmap) using geom_fruit with geom=geom_tile and axis parameters ;; 9. Reset the fill scale using new_scale_fill() ;; 10. Add the fourth layer (bar plot) using geom_fruit with geom=geom_col, axis parameters, and grid parameters
workflows.code:
trfile <- system.file("extdata", "tree.nwk", package="ggtreeExtra")
tippoint1 <- system.file("extdata", "tree_tippoint_bar.csv", package="ggtreeExtra")
ring1 <- system.file("extdata", "first_ring_discrete.csv", package="ggtreeExtra")
ring2 <- system.file("extdata", "second_ring_continuous.csv", package="ggtreeExtra")

tree <- read.tree(trfile)

dat1 <- read.csv(tippoint1)
dat2 <- read.csv(ring1)
dat3 <- read.csv(ring2)

p <- ggtree(tree, layout="fan", open.angle=10, size=0.5)

p2 <- p + 
      geom_fruit(
          data=dat1,
          geom=geom_star,
          mapping=aes(y=ID, fill=Location, size=Length, starshape=Group),
          position="identity",
          starstroke=0.2
      ) + 
      scale_size_continuous(
          range=c(1, 3),
          guide=guide_legend(
                    keywidth=0.5, 
                    keyheight=0.5,
                    override.aes=list(starshape=15),
                    order=2
                )
      ) +
      scale_fill_manual(
          values=c("#F8766D", "#C49A00", "#53B400", "#00C094", "#00B6EB", "#A58AFF", "#FB61D7"),
          guide="none" 
      ) + 
      scale_starshape_manual(
          values=c(1, 15),
          guide=guide_legend(
                    keywidth=0.5,
                    keyheight=0.5,
                    order=1
                )
      )

p3 <- p2 + 
      new_scale_fill() + 
      geom_fruit(
          data=dat2,
          geom=geom_tile,
          mapping=aes(y=ID, x=Pos, fill=Type),
          offset=0.08,
          pwidth=0.25
      ) + 
      scale_fill_manual(
          values=c("#339933", "#dfac03"),
          guide=guide_legend(keywidth=0.5, keyheight=0.5, order=3)
      ) 

p4 <- p3 + 
      new_scale_fill() +
      geom_fruit(
          data=dat3,
          geom=geom_tile,
          mapping=aes(y=ID, x=Type2, alpha=Alpha, fill=Type2),
          pwidth=0.15,
          axis.params=list(
                          axis="x",
                          text.angle=-45,
                          hjust=0
                      )
      ) +
      scale_fill_manual(
          values=c("#b22222", "#005500", "#0000be", "#9f1f9f"),
          guide=guide_legend(keywidth=0.5, keyheight=0.5, order=4)
      ) +
      scale_alpha_continuous(
          range=c(0, 0.4),
          guide=guide_legend(keywidth=0.5, keyheight=0.5, order=5)
      ) 

p5 <- p4 + 
      new_scale_fill() +
      geom_fruit(
          data=dat1,
          geom=geom_col,
          mapping=aes(y=ID, x=Abundance, fill=Location),
          pwidth=0.4,
          axis.params=list(
                          axis="x",
                          text.angle=-45,
                          hjust=0
                      ),
          grid.params=list()
      ) + 
      scale_fill_manual(
          values=c("#F8766D", "#C49A00", "#53B400", "#00C094", "#00B6EB", "#A58AFF", "#FB61D7"),
          guide=guide_legend(keywidth=0.5, keyheight=0.5, order=6)
      ) +
      theme(
          legend.background=element_rect(fill=NA),
          legend.title=element_text(size=7),
          legend.text=element_text(size=6),
          legend.spacing.y = unit(0.02, "cm")
      )

workflows.name: same_position_multiple_layers
workflows.intent: Add multiple overlapping or co-located data layers on the exact same external panel/ring of a phylogenetic tree.
input: associated_data.csv (CSV containing tip values and group classifications)
workflows.stages: 1. Generate or read a phylogenetic tree ;; 2. Prepare associated datasets with matching tip labels ;; 3. Initialize the tree plot using ggtree ;; 4. Add the first ring using geom_fruit ;; 5. Reset the fill scale using new_scale_fill() ;; 6. Add multiple layers to the second ring using geom_fruit_list, ensuring the first element is a geom_fruit layer, followed by scales and additional geom_fruit layers ;; 7. Reset the fill scale and add subsequent rings as needed
workflows.code:
set.seed(1024)
tr <- rtree(100)
dt <- data.frame(id=tr$tip.label, value=abs(rnorm(100)), group=c(rep("A",50),rep("B",50)))
df <- dt
dtf <- dt
colnames(df)[[3]] <- "group2"
colnames(dtf)[[3]] <- "group3"

p <- ggtree(tr, layout="fan", open.angle=0)

p1 <- p + 
      geom_fruit(
          data = dt,
          geom = geom_col,
          mapping = aes(y=id, x=value, fill=group),
      ) + 
      new_scale_fill()

p2 <- p1 + 
      geom_fruit_list(
          geom_fruit(
              data = df,
              geom = geom_col,
              mapping = aes(y=id, x=value, fill=group2),
          ),
          scale_fill_manual(values=c("blue", "red")),
          new_scale_fill(),
          geom_fruit(
              data = dt,
              geom = geom_star,
              mapping = aes(y=id, x=value, fill=group),
              size = 2.5,
              color = NA,
              starstroke = 0
          )
      ) + 
      new_scale_fill()

p3 <- p2 + 
      geom_fruit(
          data = dtf,
          geom = geom_col,
          mapping = aes(y=id, x=value, fill=group3)
      ) +
      scale_fill_manual(values=c("#00AED7", "#009E73"))
